_comment: THE TinyTPU-isa INSTRUCTION SET. This file is the source of truth: every
opcode number, every field position and width, the instruction memory
header, the AGU term encoding, the loop-stack semantics, the memory map,
the two program contracts, the build parameters and their legal ranges,
and the numerics. Edit here, then run:
python gen_isa.py --write     regenerate every derived artefact
python gen_isa.py --check     fail if any artefact is stale, or if
either consumer disagrees with this file
python gen_isa.py --conform   ... and check the EMITTED HLS's bit
slices against the field table
Derived artefacts (generated, checked in, verified byte-identical):
isa_encoding.py                          this file as Python: the
constants, the encoder, the decoder with the operand names below, the
control-flow/AGU resolver, the header builder and the numerics.
docs/source/designs/tinytpu_isa.rst      the ISA tables, between the
GENERATED markers; the prose around them is hand-written.
The two consumers are held to this file from OPPOSITE ends, which is the
point of having it:
* the DESIGN (microarch_isa.py, instantiating the `ip/` unit library)
names the layout once in ip/isa.py for the encoder and the
assembler, and keeps the HARDWARE's bit slices written out in
ip/units/ -- Allo cannot infer a slice's width from symbolic bounds
(infer.py:582 widens every extract to i32), so they cannot read
ip/isa.py -- and `gen_isa.py --check` holds every one of them to the
table below by value, by slice, and by behaviour.
* the REFERENCE MODEL (isa_ref.py) is built ON isa_encoding.py: it
names operands by the `name` given here and never sees a bit
position, an opcode number or a numeric width the design chose. It
used to import them from the design, which made it a restatement of
the design rather than an oracle for it.
A parameter's DEFAULT is recorded here as well as its legal range,
because the generated module has to build the SAME machine the design
builds: `gen_isa.py --check` re-imports both under several environments
and compares every parameter and derived constant. When a default moves
in the design -- the pending MAXDIM rebuild sizes the memories from
MAXDIM * MAXDIM / T -- re-derive it here rather than restating it: a
literal goes in `default`, one computed from other parameters goes in
`default_expression`.
JSON, not YAML: the generator and the conformance check must run wherever
`allo` runs, and `json` is in the standard library while PyYAML is not in
this repository's requirements. Prose lives in `_comment` and `note`
keys, as MiniTPU's docs/isa_latency.json does.
name: TinyTPU-isa

consumers.note: The spec as Python. Regenerated and diffed byte for byte by gen_isa.py --check.
The ISA tables, between the GENERATED markers. The prose around them is hand-written.

The shipped instantiation: the build parameters, read from the environment, and the names the harness imports. Held to this file by parameter range and by parameter agreement under several configurations.

Opcodes, DMA flags, AGU targets and budgets, and the instruction layout named once (OP_LO .. NR_HI, AGU_*_BITS), which `enc`/`enc_agu` build from. Held by value, layout name by layout name, and by behaviour.
`expand`, the program validator and the imem header, decoding through ip/isa.py. Held by behaviour on every program the check generates, and AR_RAW_DIST by value.

The hardware. Its bit slices of a 64-bit word are literal because a symbolic bound widens the extract to i32 (docs/source/designs/tinytpu_library.rst), so every slice is checked against the field table here, as is the mvout saturation.
The program generator, through the encoder it shares with the design.
The reference model. Names operands by the `name` given below and never sees a bit position, an opcode number or a numeric width the design chose.

_comment: Placement on the CHIA harness's frozen/editable axis: isa_spec.json,
gen_isa.py and the generated isa_encoding.py belong in FROZEN_DESIGN
/ the evaluator's FROZEN list. They judge a candidate; they are not
one. Nothing a candidate may write needs to import them, which is
what keeps spec_policy's ban on `open` and `exec` untouched.

consumers.note: `TINYTPU_ISA`: the compiler-side descriptor of what one instruction word can carry. It imports nothing from examples/, so its address_terms and loop_depth budgets are checked against `agu.terms` and `loop_stack.depth` rather than generated.

_comment: EVERY FIELD CARRIES ONE MORE BIT THAN ITS VALUE RANGE NEEDS. An N-bit
field safely carries 0 .. 2^(N-1) - 1, so the top bit is always spare.
A bit slice used to be extracted into a SIGNED ap_int<N> in the emitted
HLS, so a field whose top bit was set read back negative and a loop
bounded by it ran zero times: `nr = 64` for a 64-row `vld` silently
loaded nothing. The emitter is fixed (fork 3de74846, upstream #612,
merged dc6b8fa6) and the rule is KEPT as a conservative encoding
convention. The narrative, and why only cosim caught it, is in the
docs page under 'The spare-bit rule, and the signed bit-slice bug'.
One instruction is two 64-bit words. Word 0 is the opcode and five
fields; word 1 is the AGU terms. The fields are deliberately wider
than any legal value so that the encoding is not the limit on problem
size -- except `nr`, whose width IS load-bearing: a synthesis tool
bounds a runtime-bounded loop by the range of its index, so a 12-bit
row count made Vitis assume 4095 rows per instruction and report a
top-level latency of 91407 cycles. Narrowing the field narrows the
bound.

fields.name: op
fields.note: 6 bits for 9 opcodes; the spare-bit rule caps it at 31.

fields.name: f0
fields.note: 12 bits for a 2047 maximum, comfortably above SPAD_ROWS and NVR.

fields.name: nr
fields.role: row count, or loop trip count
fields.note: Never an AGU target, so it is the same for every dynamic issue of a static instruction. 8 bits for MAXROWS = 127.

word1.note: The AGU terms; see the `agu` section. Zero when an instruction needs no address generation.

_comment: Up to three address terms per instruction, each `(target, level,
stride)`, resolving to `field[target] += iv[level] * stride` in the
sequencer before the word is dispatched. Terms NAME their target
rather than being fixed one-per-field, because one field often needs
two: the weight `mm` inside the k loop is at `B_SP + nb*MAXDIM +
kb*T`, two terms on f3, which a one-term-per-field encoding cannot
say. Without the AGU a loop body would reissue identical addresses
and simply redo the same work.

subfields.name: target
subfields.note: 4 bits for 0..4 under the spare-bit rule.

agu.semantics: field[target] += iv[level] * stride, for each term with target != 0, in term order
rules: A term may only name a loop level that is OPEN at that instruction; the sequencer would otherwise resolve it against a stale iv_now[level].
loop, endloop and nop carry no AGU terms.

The sequencer writes the resolved sum back into the 12-bit field, so a term can push a field past what the encoder would have accepted on its own; `check_program` is the only place that sees the resolved value.

_comment: loop/endloop bound a body and the PC branches backward, so the STATIC
program is O(nesting) while the DYNAMIC instruction stream is
O(tiles). A LIFO of {body_start, iv, trip} frames, LOOP_DEPTH levels
deep, modelled on MiniTPU's sequencer_loop_ctrl.
semantics: loop: push {pc+1, 0, nr}, set iv_now[level] = 0, pc += 1. The body is the instruction stream up to the matching endloop.
endloop: iv += 1; if iv < trip then iv_now[level] = iv and pc = body_start, else pop and pc += 1.
The nesting depth at which a loop opens IS the AGU level it exports.
rules: The back edge is tested AFTER the body, so a trip count of 0 still runs the body ONCE. Trip counts below 1 are refused, not silently corrected.
Loops must be balanced and nested no deeper than LOOP_DEPTH.

operands.name: mode
operands.note: 0: A -> spad, 1: B -> spad, 2: A -> vr, 3: B -> vr. The shipped GEMM uses 2 for activations and 1 for weights.

operands.name: dram_row0
operands.meaning: first DRAM row of the source matrix

operands.name: col_block
operands.meaning: packed-word column block within the row, 0 .. WPR-1

operands.name: dst_row0
operands.meaning: first destination row, in spad or vr by the mode bit

opcodes.name: dma_st
opcodes.note: Retired: results leave via mvout. `check_program` refuses it, so the number stays reserved rather than reusable.

opcodes.name: vld
opcodes.note: A pure copy. It MAY copy an unwritten spad row, but the copy is then unwritten too.

opcodes.name: mm
opcodes.rows: nr activation rows (wavefront rows through the array)

operands.name: spad_w
operands.meaning: first of T weight rows in spad

opcodes.note: PE(i, j) holds lane j of weight row i and taps lane i of the activation word, so output column j is sum_i act[i] * W[i][j].

operands.name: ar_s1
operands.meaning: first row of the left source

operands.name: ar_s2
operands.meaning: first row of the right source

opcodes.name: mvout

operands.name: col_block
operands.meaning: packed-word column block of C, 0 .. WPR-1

opcodes.note: The only way a result leaves the accelerator. Values pass through the output conversion in the numerics section.

opcodes.name: loop
opcodes.rows: nr is the trip count, minimum 1

opcodes.name: vaddrelu

operands.name: ar_s1
operands.meaning: first row of the left source

operands.name: ar_s2
operands.meaning: first row of the right source

opcodes.note: `vadd` then `vrelu` in one pass: the accumulator already has both the adder and the rectifier, so the composition costs a mux and saves a pass over `ar` and an intermediate row. Two `ar` reads a row, so two accu steps a row -- which nothing here says, because it follows from `accu` having one `ar` read port.

_comment: The sequencer sends each unit only the instructions it executes, in
DATAFLOW order: if it blocks on a full queue, every unit upstream of
the blocked one already holds its instruction and can keep producing
what the blocked unit waits for. Dispatching downstream-first
deadlocks. Two units get a REWRITTEN copy so their flat row loops can
read their own work count straight out of `nr` -- a row count that
depends on the decoded opcode is a carried dependence and closes a
flat loop at Final II = 2.
WHICH units need a rewritten `nr`, and to what, is not stated here any
more: it is every unit the sequencer dispatches to whose own work count
differs from the instruction's row count, and that follows from the
actions and the ports. `notes` keeps only the prose, keyed by
opcode/unit; adding an instruction adds no entry to either.

notes.mm/spm: One header word plus T weight rows down wcol; f1 carries the array's row count into the header word.
notes.vadd/accu: accu takes two iterations per vadd row: first source on the even one, second source and the write on the odd one. 2 * MAXROWS fits the 8-bit field.

_comment: imem[0:NHDR] is a header of per-unit WORK counts; instructions follow,
two words each. imem[0] is static and bounds the sequencer's fetch;
every other count is DYNAMIC, computed by resolving the program's
control flow at assembly time. They are work counts, not instruction
counts, because every unit runs one flat loop over the rows (or words,
or iterations) it will actually process. A unit promised the wrong
number here does not produce a wrong answer, it HANGS -- the one place
where the assembler and the microarchitecture are coupled.
Every count but the static one is now THE WORK A UNIT DOES, computed from
the actions in `opcodes` and the ports in `units` rather than restated
here: an entry names a unit (its busiest port), a unit and one port, or a
memory whose row span a burst must cover. `spm` charging an `mm` T+1 and
`accu` charging a `vadd` two steps a row used to be two sentences in this
file and are now consequences of `spm` putting T+1 words down `wcol` and
of `accu` having one `ar` read port.

entries.name: n_instr
entries.note: Bounds the fetch loop: the sequencer stops when pc >= n_instr.

entries.name: spm_rows
entries.note: A dma_ld counts for spm or for vru by its destination bit, never both.

entries.name: mm_count
entries.consumer: the array, via spm's header word

entries.name: mm_rows
entries.consumer: the array, via spm's header word
entries.note: Each PE's own flat trip count: every wavefront row of every mm.

entries.name: a_span
entries.note: The DRAM row span dma_ld must burst for A: the highest row any of its dma_lds names once the AGU is resolved.

constraints: IMEM_SIZE % 8 == 0 -- the program prefetch moves 8 words per iteration.
NHDR + IWORDS * len(prog) <= IMEM_SIZE for every program that runs.
size.note: The prefetch is IMEM_SIZE words long whatever the program, so every unused slot is startup time. Sized to the longest program shipped, not to a round number.

memories.name: spad
memories.row_contents: T int8 lanes, one packed word
memories.note: Pure SIMD access: an address names a whole packed word and there is no way to address a lane, which is what lets a single-ported memory feed T lanes per cycle.
memories.collision_note: one writer by construction: the owning unit is the memory's sole owner, so a same-element collision cannot be composed

memories.name: vr
memories.row_contents: T int8 lanes, one packed word
memories.collision_note: one writer by construction: the owning unit is the memory's sole owner, so a same-element collision cannot be composed

memories.name: ar
memories.collision_note: one writer by construction: the owning unit is the memory's sole owner, so a same-element collision cannot be composed

memories.name: imem
memories.row_contents: header words, then two words per instruction
memories.note: Prefetched on-chip in full by one burst before anything runs, so it cannot be read early.

memories.name: A
memories.row_contents: int8, flat, addressed row * MAXDIM + col

memories.name: B
memories.row_contents: int8, flat, addressed row * MAXDIM + col

memories.name: C
memories.row_contents: int8, flat, addressed row * MAXDIM + col
memories.note: Rows and column blocks no mvout names are left exactly as the host passed them, which is how a sentinel check falls out of comparing the whole of C.

_comment: spad, vr and ar are NOT cleared by the hardware -- their zero
initialisers were removed to delete a 514-cycle memset -- so at
ap_start each holds whatever the previous invocation, or power-up,
left there. The guarantee moved from the hardware to the program.
rules: Every ar row read by an accumulating mm, by either source of a vadd, by a vrelu source or by an mvout must have been written earlier in the SAME program, by an overwriting mm, a vadd or a vrelu.
Every vr row an mm reads as activations, and every spad row it reads as weights, must hold data a dma_ld put there -- directly, or into spad and then through a vld.
vld is a pure copy and may copy an unwritten spad row; the copy is then unwritten too, and consuming it in an mm is an error.
nr >= 1 on every data op: a unit fetches an instruction whenever its row counter runs out, so a zero-row instruction is fetched as if it had one row. It desynchronises the unit; it is not a no-op.
Every resolved field must be within 0 .. 2047, the range the encoding rule admits.
write_before_read.enforced_by: microarch_isa.check_program, which microarch_isa.assemble calls, so a violating program cannot be assembled
write_before_read.not_enforced_by_hardware: Reading an accumulator row early is a wrong answer, not a crash.
write_before_read.note: dma_ld's burst buffers and the sequencer's program buffer are unzeroed too, but cannot be read early and so carry no obligation: the program buffer is filled by one unconditional IMEM_SIZE-word burst, and the A and B spans in the header are computed from the same resolved trace that names the rows dma_ld reads.

_comment: accu runs at II=1 because schedule() tells Vitis there is no carried
dependence through ar. THAT CLAIM IS NOT TRUE OF THE HARDWARE ON ITS
OWN: in the synthesized loop the ar load issues in pipeline state 5
and the store lands in state 7. The assembler makes it true by
refusing programs that read a row too soon. The measured window, the
cosim evidence and what the claim bought in flip-flops are in the
docs page under 'The accumulator's dependence claim'.

iteration_cost.vadd: 2 per row: first source on the even iteration, second source and the write on the odd one

accumulator_raw_distance.rule: A read of an ar row must come at least AR_RAW_DIST accu iterations after the write it depends on.
constraints: AR_RAW_DIST <= T, so no GEMM is constrained by it -- the smallest GEMM has T rows.
accumulator_raw_distance.exercised_at_its_edge_by: isa_dsl.ar_distance_program(AR_RAW_DIST), run by TPU_TB=stress cosim on every build

parameters.name: T
parameters.role: SIMD width, and the array dimension: the array is T*T processing elements
constraints: T >= 4, so a packed operand word has room for the two 16-bit counts spm sends down wcol.
MAXDIM % T == 0, so a DRAM row is a whole number of packed words.
parameters.note: The one parameter that changes the SHAPE of the generated region: T*T kernel instances and T, T*T stream arrays.

parameters.name: MAXDIM
parameters.role: largest M, K, N supported by one build
parameters.note: Both ceilings are the encoding, not the datapath, and `isa_encoding.maxdim_ceiling` computes each rather than restating it; see maxdim_ceilings for which question each answers. The design ships at 64, inside both.

parameters.name: SPAD_ROWS
constraints: SPAD_ROWS <= 2047, the range a 12-bit field admits under the encoding rule
parameters.note: Derived, not typed in. The shipped GEMM lays B out at B_SP + nb*MAXDIM + k, so the highest row it names is OPERAND_ROWS; the TEST_WINDOW floor is there because the fuzz programs address a fixed 64-row window independently of MAXDIM.

parameters.name: NVR
parameters.note: Derived from the same layout: A sits at A_VR + kb*MAXDIM + m. Three independent literals here were silently too small above MAXDIM=16 -- the build assembled and gave wrong answers.

parameters.name: NAR
parameters.note: AR_C is MAXDIM rows and AR_P another MAXDIM from MAXDIM+1, so a GEMM plus a vector program needs 2*MAXDIM+2; the 128 floor keeps the fixed-address test programs legal at small MAXDIM.

parameters.name: QD
parameters.role: stream depth on every point-to-point channel
parameters.note: Not an ISA fact; listed because it is a TPU_* build parameter and a build must report it.

parameters.name: DMA_WORDS
parameters.default_expression: min(WPR, max(1, BUS_BYTES // (VW // 8))) if os.environ.get("TPU_DMA_WIDEN") == "1" else 1
parameters.role: packed words the operand burst moves per loop iteration
parameters.note: Not an ISA fact; listed because it is a TPU_* build parameter, a build must report it, and TPU_DMA_WIDEN selects it indirectly.

_comment: Facts that FOLLOW from the sections above rather than being stated
in them, and that `gen_isa.py --check` recomputes from the spec and
then confirms against the design. They are here because all three
were documented wrongly in this project until 2026-09-21, and nothing
checked them: a property nothing computes is a sentence, not a spec.

derived_properties.statement: Every operand field is a legal AGU target, including one with a restricted value set such as mm's `acc`. Nothing in the encoding or in the sequencer distinguishes them: the sequencer adds iv[level] * stride to whichever field the term names and writes the sum back, and it does not know which fields have restricted values.
derived_properties.corrects: Three documents in this project described `acc` as a static field that cannot be predicated on an induction variable. That is false. The real obstacle is the next property.

derived_properties.statement: An AGU term contributes base + iv * stride with no predication, no saturation and no wrap, so the values a field takes over a loop of trip t are the arithmetic progression base, base + stride, ..., base + (t-1) * stride, and nothing bends it back inside a bound. A field with a restricted value set is therefore drivable from a loop for exactly as long as that progression stays inside the set -- `isa_encoding.agu_legal_trip` computes how long from `legal_values` alone.
derived_properties.note: At base 0 stride 1 the frontier is 2: an accumulate field driven by the reduce loop assembles for exactly two k-tiles and is rejected at the third.

derived_properties.statement: A term on `acc` costs one of the AGU_TERMS terms an instruction carries. The accumulating mm of the shipped tiled GEMM already spends all of them -- activations walk the reduce loop, weights walk both the column loop and the reduce loop -- so driving `acc` from the reduce loop needs one more than the instruction word has, and the budget refuses the instruction before the monotonicity frontier above is ever reached. Widening the address generator and relieving `acc` are therefore COMPLEMENTS, not alternatives: at AGU_TERMS = 3 the second constraint is unreachable for any program with a column loop.
derived_properties.note: `terms_used_by_shipped_acc_mm` is read out of the shipped program's own AGU word, not restated here.

derived_properties.statement: What bounds MAXDIM is the ENCODING, not the datapath, and both bounds follow from numbers already in this file. They answer different questions -- one asks what the operand layout can ADDRESS, the other what a CUBIC GEMM's header count can promise -- so neither is a correction of the other, and the binding one depends on the program. `isa_encoding.maxdim_ceiling` computes each over multiples of T, and the design refuses a cubic GEMM at exactly the value the cubic-header ceiling gives.
derived_properties.note: The numbers are computed, not typed: at T=4 the addressing ceiling is 88 and the cubic-header ceiling is 76, so the cubic one binds; at T=8 they are 128 and 120, so the cubic one binds there too. An earlier revision of this file said 90 for the first, copied from the design's comment, which solved the inequality over the reals instead of over multiples of T.

derived_properties.statement: The limits in `program_limits` decide exactly which GEMM shapes this build can run, and `isa_encoding.gemm_limits` computes which limit refuses a shape and by how much. For the shipped layout, a shape assembles if and only if every limit but the `split_operand_load` alternative fits.
derived_properties.note: The `split_operand_load` row is the one that makes the answer actionable rather than final: at T=8 MAXDIM=128 the shipped layout is over by 1 on `max(M, K)` for 32x128x128 and 64x128x128, but splitting the B load removes K from the row count and both assemble and compute A@B exactly -- measured on the design, not argued. 128x128x128 is over by 1 even then, and its accu header count is over by 2049, so it needs both a wider nr and a wider header slice.
derived_properties.not_proved: At both shipped configurations the `nr` limit bites before the header-count limit for every shape the shipped layout can emit, so widening `header_counts.accu` here changes no prediction and this property does not catch it. The header bound has its teeth in `the_maxdim_ceilings_are_the_encoding's` instead, which probes MAXDIM=88 at T=4 where the cubic GEMM is refused by the header alone. It is the same shape of masking as the AGU budget hiding the monotonicity frontier: a second constraint that is never reached because a first one refuses first. Worth knowing before anyone widens `nr` and expects the shapes to follow.

assertions.why: a packed operand word must hold the two 16-bit counts spm sends down wcol
a DRAM row must be a whole number of packed words
an address field carries 11 usable bits, and the layout numbers its rows 0 .. OPERAND_ROWS-1, so the highest address must be <= 2047
a T-row GEMM must satisfy the accumulator distance contract
the program prefetch moves 8 words per iteration
imem must hold the header and at least one instruction
a 12-bit address field carries 0..2047 under the encoding rule, and a memory of depth D is addressed 0..D-1, so D <= 2048 -- the same count-versus-address distinction as the addressing ceiling
an operand memory smaller than the layout addresses assembles and gives wrong answers
AR_C is MAXDIM rows and AR_P another MAXDIM from MAXDIM+1
the operand burst moves at least one packed word per iteration

derived_constants.name: VW
derived_constants.role: packed operand word: T operand lanes

derived_constants.name: AW
derived_constants.role: packed accumulator word: T accumulator lanes

derived_constants.name: WPR
derived_constants.role: packed words per DRAM row; the legal range of col_block

derived_constants.name: OPERAND_ROWS
derived_constants.role: the highest operand row the shipped GEMM's layout names; what the operand memories are sized from

derived_constants.name: TEST_WINDOW
derived_constants.role: the fixed row window the stress harness's fuzz programs address, independently of MAXDIM; a floor under the operand memories

derived_constants.name: BUS_BYTES
derived_constants.role: the m_axi beat the build aligns to (align_value 64)

derived_constants.name: MAXROWS
derived_constants.role: the largest nr the 8-bit field admits under the encoding rule

_comment: One entry per arithmetic configuration the design can be built in, and
`active` names the one this revision ships. A new configuration (bf16
operands with a 24-bit float accumulator, say) is ADDED as a sibling
with the same keys -- operand, accumulator, multiply, accumulate,
output -- and nothing above has to move. Every claim here is about
VALUES, not about widths: `exact` means the result is the exact
mathematical one, and where it is not, `rounding` and `overflow` say
what happens instead. That distinction is the reason this section
exists: with int8 operands every statement below is `exact` and any
model agrees with any other, which hides whether the model and the
design agree for the right reason.
Order of accumulation is stated because it stops being irrelevant the
moment the accumulator rounds: the array sums strictly sequentially
down a PE column, in ascending contraction index, never as a tree.

operand.where: A, B, C at the region boundary; spad and vr lanes

accumulator.where: ar lanes, and the partial sum travelling south through the array

multiply.note: int8 x int8 is bounded by 128*128 = 16384, so a 16-bit product is exact and the multiplier stays narrow.

accumulate.order: strictly sequential in ascending contraction index, south down the PE column, then the mm's acc term
accumulate.note: Exact for every value that fits; a sum that does not fit wraps rather than saturating. With int8 operands and T <= 127 a single mm cannot overflow, but an accumulating chain of mms can, and so can a vadd.

output.where: mvout, in accu, before the word leaves for dma_st
output.note: Gemmini's mvout under ACC_SCALE_IDENTITY with shift 0, which is what its allo_cmp.c passes.

_comment: TWO ceilings bound MAXDIM, they answer DIFFERENT questions, and neither
is architectural -- both are the ENCODING. `isa_encoding.maxdim_ceiling`
computes each one rather than restating it, because the search must run
over MULTIPLES OF T (`MAXDIM % T == 0` is an assertion above). Solving
either inequality over the reals gives a number no build can use: that
is how `MAXDIM <= 90` came to be written into microarch_isa.py, into
docs/source/designs/benchmarks.rst and into an earlier revision of this
file, when the answer at T=4 is 88. The formula was also written
`MAXDIM**2 / T`, which is not what the layout computes -- it is
`(MAXDIM // T) * MAXDIM`, and the two differ exactly when MAXDIM is not
a multiple of T, which is the case the wrong answer rested on.

The off-by-one is worth the sentence: an earlier revision here wrote `OPERAND_ROWS <= 2047`, confusing a COUNT with the highest ADDRESS. It gave the right answer at T=4 by luck and the wrong one at T=8, and the conformance check found it by disagreeing with the design.

The same off-by-one appeared TWICE: once in the addressing ceiling and once in the memory-depth bound, both writing 2047 where a DEPTH (or a row count) is bounded by 2048 because its highest ADDRESS is 2047. Both gave the right answer at T=4 and the wrong one at T=8 MAXDIM=128, which is exactly the configuration a cross-team comparison turned on. Count versus highest address is the distinction to check first whenever a bound here is a power of two minus one.

Only the ADDRESSING ceiling is a build invariant; the cubic-header one is not, and asserting it at import would refuse a build that is fine for every shape but the largest cube. `check_parameters` therefore asserts the first and not the second, and the second lives here and in program_limits.header_counts, where it is checked per program by `assemble`.

ceilings.name: addressing
ceilings.question: How large a MAXDIM can the shipped GEMM's operand layout ADDRESS? A property of the layout and the address field, independent of the shape being run.
ceilings.from: an address field carries 11 usable bits (encoding_rule), so the highest operand ADDRESS must be <= 2047. The layout names OPERAND_ROWS rows, numbered 0 .. OPERAND_ROWS-1, so the bound is OPERAND_ROWS <= 2048 -- the design's import-time assert says the same thing. Writing it as OPERAND_ROWS <= 2047 is off by one and understates the ceiling at T=8 (120 instead of 128).
ceilings.fails_as: check_program: "AGU-resolved f3=... is outside the 0..2047 range", or the import-time assert on OPERAND_ROWS

ceilings.name: cubic_header
ceilings.question: How large a MAXDIM can a CUBIC GEMM's header count promise accu? A property of the WORKLOAD as well as the encoding -- a non-cubic shape gives a different count, so this ceiling moves with the program.
ceilings.from: a header count is read back through a 15-bit slice (imem.count_slice_width), and accu's iteration count for an MxMxM GEMM is M**3/T**2 + M**2/T
ceilings.fails_as: assemble: "header count ... does not fit 15 bits"

maxdim_ceilings.note: The binding ceiling for a build is the smaller of the two, and which one binds depends on the program. The design ships at MAXDIM=64, inside both.

_comment: Limits on what a PROGRAM may ask for, as opposed to what a BUILD may be
configured to. They are not interchangeable, and conflating them is an
error this file made: `MAXDIM <= MAXROWS` was asserted at build level,
which would refuse a MAXDIM=128 build outright. The design asserts no
such thing -- it imports fine at MAXDIM=128 and simply cannot run the
shapes whose row counts overflow `nr`.

Each limit carries a `need` and an `allowed` expression over (M, K, N, T) and this build's constants, so `isa_encoding.gemm_limits(M, K, N)` computes which limit refuses a shape and BY HOW MUCH. The margin is the point: `short by one in nr` is a design target, `cannot express` is not.

limits.name: build_extent
limits.rule: No dimension may exceed the build's MAXDIM.

limits.name: rows_per_instruction.shipped_layout
limits.rule: The shipped tiled-GEMM layout issues one dma_ld of K rows per B column block and one mm of M rows per tile, so both M and K travel in `nr`.
limits.enforced_by: isa_dsl.gemm_program's assert, and `enc` on the word itself
limits.note: A property of THIS LAYOUT, not of the ISA.

limits.name: rows_per_instruction.split_operand_load
limits.rule: Splitting the B load into several dma_lds removes K from the row count; only M still travels in `nr`. The instruction set permits this -- the shipped generator simply does not emit it.
limits.note: Measured: at T=8 MAXDIM=128 this makes 32x128x128 and 64x128x128 assemble and compute A@B exactly, where the shipped layout refuses both.

limits.name: header_counts.accu
limits.rule: accu's per-unit work count is read back through a 15-bit slice. It is the largest header count, and it depends on the SHAPE, not only on MAXDIM.

_comment: THE UNITS, AS PORTS AND A STEP RATE. An instruction's per-unit cost is
not written down anywhere in this file: it FOLLOWS from the actions
below and these ports. `vadd` costs `accu` two steps a row because it
reads `ar` twice and `accu` has one `ar` read port, not because anyone
typed 2. Read and write ports are counted separately because they do
not cost the same -- MiniTPU measured a third read port at +592 LUT and
a second write port at 4.3x the LUTs plus a timing miss, and our own
ASIC flow hit the same asymmetry in ELAB-366.
`ii` is the cycles between a unit's steps and `elastic` says what
happens when an issue needs more cycles than one step: a flat work loop
spends another step, a body that must retire every `ii` cycles cannot
and the composition is refused instead. `allo/actions.py` holds the
rule; `docs/source/developer/actions.rst` says why a port count without
an initiation interval decides a two-store loop wrongly in BOTH
directions.

list.name: sequencer
list.note: The program counter and the loop stack. Only `loop` and `endloop` are its own work; every other opcode it dispatches.

list.name: spm
list.note: One spad access per step at a muxed address, which a dual-port BRAM holds at II=1.

list.name: array
list.note: `wld` and `pe`, T x T of each. They decode no instruction; the counts they run on arrive in spm's header word. The reduction down each column is the `p_fwd` chain, which is the unit GRAPH rather than a declaration -- see the doc page on what this model cannot say about it.

list.name: accu

ports.name: alu
ports.note: Two CHAINED lane operations per step. `vadd` and `vrelu` use one; `vaddrelu` uses both, which is exactly what fusing them into one accumulator pass claims. It is a TIMING claim about combinational depth, not a count of anything, so it is the one number here that has to be measured against synthesis rather than declared -- raise it far enough and the model will happily compose an instruction the clock cannot close.

list.note: Every arm is muxed down to one `ar` read and one `ar` write per step. Its II=1 rests on a dependence claim the assembler makes true, not on the hardware.
